page.layout: One page of text. Above the text, two oval medallion illustrations side by side (a male and a female bust). Running head at top centre. Page number at top right. Running text in one column below the illustrations. Signature mark at the foot, right of the text. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: IUSTINIANUS, Iustini ex sorore nepos, ab avunculo, paulò ante obitum successor instituitur, imperatq; anno mundi 4491. à Christo nato 529. Hic Romani imperij gloriam Plurimum ampliavit. Primùm Persæ, Belisarij opera, intra suos fi-nes cōtinuit, fudit, fugavit, trans Eufrate abire coëgit: iura imperij toto Orieti posuit: Belisarium cum victoria redeuntem, & aureo curru triumphantem Iustinianus magno plausu excepit. Inde eodem duce Romā à Gothorum servitute asseruit: Africa quoque recuperata, Gelimerem, Vandalorum Regem, catenis vinctum Constantinopolim misit Belisarius: triumphus maior Persico fuit. Narsete duce, occupato aliunde Belisario, tandem Gothos deleuit Iustinianus. Leges, fusissimè antea dispersas, opera Triboniani cōtraxit: Institutionū libros quatuor edidit: Codicem invulgavit. Maximus sanè princeps, nisi avariciæ, & delirij Eutychiani reus fuisset: Serici usus è Persis ad Græcos hoc tempore trāsiit, jampridè desitus. Moritur morbo, & mente captus, anno ætatis &c. imperij 38. Pom. Læt. Pau. Diaco. lib. 7. & 8. Egna. lib. 2. Eutr. auctus lib. 16. autor est, Iustinianum morte præventum cum edictum ubiq; à pietate alienum transmisisset.

THEODORA uxor fuit Iustiniani, ex quo matrem Iu-stinæ suscepit Iustinianus. Hæc fraudē molita est in Sylverium Papam, quem Belisarius falsit testibus convictū in exilium misit, ubi etiam mortuus est. consulito Eutropium auctum li. 16.

page.notes: Two medallions above the text: left, a bust in profile facing right of a man with a laurel-type headband, inscription around the rim reading "IVSTINIANVS · PP · AVG" (partly worn: "D" and "IVSTINIANVS" letters on the left rim read as "IVSTINIANVS"). Right, a bust in profile facing right of a woman with braided hair, inscription around the rim reading "IVSTINIANI · THEODORA" with "VXOR" at the lower left. The text of the rim inscriptions is part of an illustration and is not transcribed. Doubtful: "Iustinæ" and "Hæc fraudē" read from a slightly blurred print. Possible printing error: "Sylverium" is printed "Syluerium" in the original; spelling kept with y, u/v corrected.
